content: This medication, a combination of ledipasvir and sofosbuvir, is used to treat chronic hepatitis C, a viral infection affecting the liver. It may sometimes be prescribed alongside another antiviral medication, ribavirin. These drugs work by reducing the amount of hepatitis C virus in the body, helping the immune system combat the infection and potentially aiding liver recovery. However, it is not known if this treatment prevents the transmission of the virus to others. Before starting ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to either drug or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you have diabetes, hepatitis C treatment may lower your blood sugar levels, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Your doctor may need to adjust your diabetes treatment plan accordingly. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. If used in combination with ribavirin, it must not be taken during pregnancy by either the pregnant woman or her male partner, as it may harm an unborn baby. Reliable birth control methods must be used when at least one sexual partner is taking these medications together. Female patients should continue using birth control for nine months after stopping treatment, while male patients should continue for six months. It is unknown if this medication passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This medication can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting their efficacy. Similarly, other medications can impact the removal of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir from your body, which may influence its effectiveness. Examples of interacting drugs include apalutamide, rifamycins (such as rifampin or rifabutin), and St. John’s wort. Always keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Common side effects of this medication include tiredness, headache, nausea, diarrhea, or difficulty sleeping. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. If you experience severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 or seek emergency medical attention immediately. For non-emergency overdoses, contact a poison control center (U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222). Laboratory tests, such as liver function tests and tests for hepatitis B and C, should be conducted before starting this medication, during treatment, and after completing it. If you are using this medication with ribavirin, it is recommended that female patients or female partners of male patients take a pregnancy test before starting treatment. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than six hours before your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Keep the tablets in their original container. For the pellet form, do not open the packets until you are ready to use them. Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
